Normally started by `make reindex` (ops/supervise.py runs it inside the job budget).
Progress is kept in var/checkpoint.json so the next run continues where the last
one stopped; a run with no checkpoint rebuilds the index from scratch.

    python3 -m reindex.worker --status   print progress

import logging

import time

def parse_args(argv):

    parser.add_argument("--source", default=str(ROOT / "data" / "docs.db"))
    parser.add_argument("--index-dir", default=str(ROOT / "var" / "index"))
    parser.add_argument("--checkpoint", default=str(ROOT / "var" / "checkpoint.json"))
    parser.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=BATCH_SIZE)
    parser.add_argument("--status", action="store_true", help="print progress and exit")
    return parser.parse_args(argv)


def show_status(args):
    state = Checkpoint(args.checkpoint).load()
    source = Source(args.source)
    total = source.count()
    source.close()
    rows = list(iter_rows(args.index_dir)) if Path(args.index_dir).exists() else []
    unique = len({row["id"] for row in rows})
    print("checkpoint : %s" % state)
    print("source     : %d live docs" % total)
    print("index      : %d rows, %d unique ids (%.1f%% of source)"
          % (len(rows), unique, 100.0 * unique / max(total, 1)))
    return 0


def run(args):
    ckpt = Checkpoint(args.checkpoint)
    state = ckpt.load()
    if state["complete"]:
        log.info("index already complete (%d docs)", state["docs"])
        return 0
    source = Source(args.source)
    store = ShardWriter(args.index_dir)
    if state["last_id"] == 0:
        log.info("no checkpoint: rebuilding index from scratch")
        store.reset()
    total = source.count()
    started = time.monotonic()
    log.info("starting after id %d (%d/%d docs done)", state["last_id"], state["docs"], total)

    for n, batch in enumerate(source.batches(start_id=state["last_id"], size=args.batch_size), 1):
        for doc in batch:
            store.add(transform_doc(doc))
        state["last_id"] = batch[-1].id
        state["docs"] += len(batch)
        ckpt.save(state)
        if n % 20 == 0:
            rate = n * args.batch_size / (time.monotonic() - started)
            log.info("progress: last_id=%d docs=%d/%d (%.0f docs/s)",
                     state["last_id"], state["docs"], total, rate)

    store.close()
    state["complete"] = True
    ckpt.save(state)
    source.close()
    log.info("reindex complete: %d docs", state["docs"])
    return 0

    if args.status:
        return show_status(args)
    return run(args)

"""Document -> index row.

Row format (consumed by the search service; do not change without a format bump):
  id        source doc id
  slug      url slug from the title
  lang      language code
  length    number of index tokens (stopwords removed)
  terms     up to 8 most frequent tokens, ties broken alphabetically
  checksum  sha256 prefix over the normalised title + body (change detection)
  minhash   64 x 32-bit minhash values over character 5-grams (near-duplicate detection)
"""
import hashlib
import re
import unicodedata
from collections import Counter

TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9]+")
STOPWORDS = frozenset("a an and are as at be by for from has in is it of on or that the to was "
                      "were will with".split())
TOP_TERMS = 8
NUM_PERM = 64
SHINGLE = 5
_SALTS = [b"perm-%04d" % i for i in range(NUM_PERM)]


def normalize(text):
    """NFKD-fold accents away and lowercase."""
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", text)
    return "".join(ch for ch in text if not unicodedata.combining(ch)).lower()


def tokenize(text):
    return [tok for tok in TOKEN_RE.findall(normalize(text)) if tok not in STOPWORDS]


def slugify(title):
    return "-".join(TOKEN_RE.findall(normalize(title)))[:64] or "untitled"


def checksum(title, body):
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    digest.update(normalize(title).encode("utf-8"))
    digest.update(b"\x00")
    digest.update(normalize(body).encode("utf-8"))
    return digest.hexdigest()[:32]


def minhash(tokens):
    text = " ".join(tokens)
    shingles = {text[i:i + SHINGLE] for i in range(max(1, len(text) - SHINGLE + 1))}
    encoded = [s.encode("utf-8") for s in sorted(shingles)]
    blake = hashlib.blake2b
    signature = []
    for salt in _SALTS:
        signature.append(min(int.from_bytes(blake(s, digest_size=4, salt=salt).digest(), "big")
                             for s in encoded))
    return signature


def transform_doc(doc):
    tokens = tokenize(doc.title + " " + doc.body)
    top = sorted(Counter(tokens).items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0]))[:TOP_TERMS]
    return {
        "id": doc.id,
        "slug": slugify(doc.title),
        "lang": doc.lang,
        "length": len(tokens),
        "terms": [term for term, _ in top],
        "checksum": checksum(doc.title, doc.body),
        "minhash": minhash(tokens),

## Resume and recovery

`last_id` is the last **committed** document ID (not an offset or the next ID).
The worker resumes strictly after it, preserving the source's gaps and deleted-row
filtering. SIGTERM, SIGINT, and SIGHUP request a stop between documents; the worker
commits the finished prefix and exits 75 when incomplete.

A commit first flushes and fsyncs shard data and directory entries, then atomically
replaces and fsyncs the checkpoint. The checkpoint includes a `position` containing
the final shard number and byte offset. On restart, that shard is truncated to the
committed offset and any later shards are removed before appending new work.
Thus a hard kill can discard uncommitted work but cannot skip committed rows or
replay rows into duplicates. Shard boundaries have no semantic meaning; a resumed
run starts a new shard. A completed checkpoint is idempotent.

Old checkpoints without a durable position cannot be trusted (the old writer
checkpointed buffered rows); they trigger a one-time rebuild. Malformed checkpoints
or missing committed bytes fail closed rather than silently resetting progress.
Use `./jobs clean` only when intentionally requesting a new full rebuild.

> ## Resume and recovery
>
> `last_id` is the last **committed** document ID (not an offset or the next ID).
> The worker resumes strictly after it, preserving the source's gaps and deleted-row

>
> A commit first flushes and fsyncs shard data and directory entries, then atomically
> replaces and fsyncs the checkpoint. The checkpoint includes a `position` containing
> the final shard number and byte offset. On restart, that shard is truncated to the
> committed offset and any later shards are removed before appending new work.
> Thus a hard kill can discard uncommitted work but cannot skip committed rows or
> replay rows into duplicates. Shard boundaries have no semantic meaning; a resumed
> run starts a new shard. A completed checkpoint is idempotent.
>

> checkpointed buffered rows); they trigger a one-time rebuild. Malformed checkpoints
